releases.body:
**A thread send now reaches a session that is not running, on this device or on another of your devices, and starts it.** It needs senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo pins it), and device service 0.1.31 or later on both devices for a wake from another device. A reply to a sender on another device reads only that device's sessions instead of the whole account listing; a send to a live session that is paused or holds a Stop answers `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "hold", device }`; and `waiting_on.kind` in a `thread_send` result can be `approval`, `hold` or `wake`. ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))

### Changed

- `omo remote enable` now sets the device up in one command after `omo login`. It installs the OmO device service when none runs, registers this omo's agent dir with it, turns remote sessions on, and installs and starts the always-on session host unit. If you signed in before the device service was installed, it also links that sign-in to the service, so `omo login` then `omo remote enable` leaves the device connected. Running it again changes nothing that is already in place (#13594). ([#13602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13602)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- `omo remote status` also shows this device's own units as the service manager reports them: the session host unit (running, enabled, pinned host), the device service's unit, whether the cold-wake entry is in place, and the agent dir omo registers. With `--json` these are a `local` object beside the status fields (#13594). ([#13602](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13602)) ([#13606](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13606))
- Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running is on (#13037). It runs on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (omo now pins it), the release whose session release drops a woken session's retained record. A message from another of your devices wakes a session here once both devices run device service 0.1.31 or later. The local omo daemon (`omo daemon run`, or the device service's cold-wake unit) registers this device's agent dir with the device service and takes deliveries as soon as it starts, with no session open. ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the operator daemon declares the delivery consumer as soon as it loads omo, with no session open (#13037 cold wake). `omo daemon run` sends the daemon it ensured senpi's `warm`, so a daemon the device service starts on demand can be handed deliveries before any session runs. A warm that is refused or unsupported prints one line and the run still exits 0. ([#13596](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13596)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: the session wake loads from its own sidecar (`extensions/omo-wake.js` behind `#omo-wake-runtime`): the carrier, the delivery consumer and the device-service client never enter the main `omo.js` bundle, which carries only lazy shells; the ensured host's idle-exit setting is read inside the sidecar. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: waking a session that is not running needs no setting (#13037). A `thread_send` from this machine to a session here that is not running now starts it by default, and the answer is `queued` with `waiting_on: { kind: "wake" }`. `session_wake.same_device` stays in the configuration schema only as an explicit opt-out (`false`), read for the target session's own project. The wake starts on senpi 2026.11.15-2 or later (senpi#6449), which omo now pins. ([#13456](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13456)) ([#13599](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13599))
- Thread gateway: when no operator host is running, a session that

The builtin `architect` category now defaults to Claude Fable 5.2 at thinking level `xhigh` instead of `max`: both chain rungs (the 5.2 lead and the 5.1 fallback, kept as the fallback at the same effort) carry `xhigh`, verified against the engine model catalog per the #9378 rule. Docs that spell the builtin default follow. Other categories, agent chains, and model profiles are unchanged (#13543). ([#13545](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13545)) ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

**Memory sync names the last unexplained "authority is unavailable" causes, and its log stays free of memory text.** When closing a sync operation, releasing its claim, or the request handler itself failed, Settings still showed the bare "Memory sync authority is unavailable." with nothing in the log. These now carry a code (`close_failed`, `release_failed`, `handler_failed`) and log a warning. Logged errors name the error type, not its message; only a sync service error keeps its service code and status, because other messages can quote memory content. A device or pending-request read whose failure returns after the service refused a request is logged again. Carried by the next train top's bundle regeneration. ([#13332](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13332), follow-up to #13157) ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

**A signed-out desktop no longer looks like a memory-sync error to the engine.** When the desktop had no signed-in account, the engine's main thread treated the desktop's refusal as a broken channel and the sync runner reported an error; it now reads it as signed out, as session Workers already did, and picks up the account once you sign in. Carried by the next train top's bundle regeneration. ([#13329](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13329), follow-up to #13325) ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

**Memory sync keeps working when you sign out and back in on the desktop.** Signing out and signing in again (with the same or another account) while the engine runs used to leave Settings > Memory > Sync on "Memory sync authority is unavailable." until the engine restarted. The engine now ends only the old account when the desktop retires it, ends that account's open sync sessions once, and picks up the new account on the next status read. It needs a desktop that keeps the private channel open across the rollover; with an older desktop the behaviour is unchanged. Carried by the next train top's bundle regeneration. ([#13327](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13327), fixes #13325) ([#13563](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13563))

**`omo remote` accepts `--` to end its options.** `omo remote send <device>/<session> -- --text that starts with dashes` now sends that text, and the same works for a model id given to `omo remote model`; before, any argument starting with `--` was refused as an unknown option. Options before `--` still apply. ([#13496](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13496), fixes #13431)

**The `omo remote` reference matches the command again.** It lists `open`, `send`, `model`, `interrupt` and `close` with their flags, and describes `attach` as a view you can type into; it no longer says the attach view is observe-only. The Senpi plugin README lists all 27 skills it ships (it said 19). ([#13492](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13492), fixes #13433)

**`omo remote --help` and `omo remote <command> --help` now answer.** They print the usage (or that command's entry with its flags) on stdout and exit 0, before any sign-in or device-service check, instead of failing as an unknown argument. `omo --help` lists `remote` among the commands. `-h` now also answers as a help flag after any verb, including in a value position (for example `omo remote open dev --project --help` prints help instea

**Plain `omo login` signs a computer in from the terminal while OmO accounts are closed.** A computer with no OmO desktop app — a server over SSH, a fresh Linux box — runs `omo login`, gets a device code to approve on another device, and stores the credential in the OS credential store; the attach-before-mint refusal (#13096) answers a computer that already has its device before anything is asked of the service. The success line names the signed-in account (`Signed in to OmO as <email>.`), and `omo whoami` names it too; a failed account read still says how to see it. `omo logout` and `omo whoami` run while closed, so no message names a command that refuses. `login --help` describes the route (the command stays hidden from `omo --help`), every other closed `login` form refuses with a message that names the route, the closed hints name both routes, and the compiled entry classifies bare `login`, `logout` and `whoami` as one-shot launches with the same shared parse the command uses (`login --` included). The damaged-item message names the terminal route too instead of a desktop-app-only dead end. Tests run the flow through the npm launcher (against a service-auth bundle built from this source into a temp copy of the launcher tree), the compiled entry and the toolkit CLI, with an isolated HOME and runtime dir, no inherited session bus, an injected store, and a refusal-text assertion on every zero-mint case. ([#13281](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13281)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))

**The computer-use conformance preflight tests pass on Windows.** The missing-driver message now prints its repo-relative path with forward slashes on every OS, so a run reads the same on every host, and the stdio-probe test builds its stand-in engine as a real executable for the host instead of a POSIX shell script. QA tooling only; no runtime behaviour changes. ([#13295](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13295), part of #13221)

**Computer use gets a declared-outcome conformance catalog for its QA.** `script/qa/computer/conformance/` adds a typed catalog in which every action, toolkit and mode cell on each OS declares that it delivers or refuses with an exact engine code, a report that fails a missing, duplicate, skipped or mis-coded cell or one that disturbed the person's session, an environment preflight that ends a broken host's run as `ENVIRONMENT_ERROR`, and twelve model-free reference tasks. QA tooling only; no runtime behaviour changes. ([#13241](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13241), part of #13221)

**The desktop session's actionability wait test no longer fails on a busy host.** The battery's wait now runs on an injectable clock: the host's monotonic time in a session, as before, and the fake backend's own clock in the test. So `the_battery_waits_for_an_element_that_appears_enabled_after_500_ms` checks the 500 ms wait in fake time instead of wall-clock bounds that host load could break. Runtime behaviour does not change. ([#13180](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13180), fixes #13178)

**A fuzzy handoff no longer fails on an account with many ended sessions, and never goes to a different session than an exact name would.** A fuzzy handoff first tries the thread's exact id, alias or name across every session, ended ones on other devices included, so a name that exactly matches one session always reaches that session. Otherwise local, live and ended sessions are compared together and the clearly best match wins wherever it lives; two equally good matches ask you to pick. Ended sessions that cannot match no longer count against the 500-candidate fuzzy cap, so a large history no longer blocks a unique match. ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141), follows #13066)

**A thread whose alias claim asks for a sign-in after it was created is still named by the alias.** When the account token expi

**OmO runs on senpi 2026.11.10-2.** A client can read and edit the workspace's instruction files over RPC through `read_project_file` / `write_project_file` (senpi#6307), a built session can be parked and handed out through `claim_session` (senpi#6350), the Fable 5.2 prompt preset gains the codebase-ownership sentence (senpi#6360), `generate_image` is eval-only like `bash` (senpi#6272), eval cells reach every eval-only tool through `tool.<name>(...)` and the `agent()`/`output()` helpers (senpi#6276), and the EQ goldens carry the new prompt (senpi#6355). ([#13054](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13054))

**An agent that answered a message from another agent can keep answering it in the turns the engine starts on its own, with no prompt.** The reply allowance a consumed delivery grants (a reply to that sender by id or stated name, approved from the delivery alone) now lasts for the work the delivery started: the consuming turn and every later turn the engine starts by itself - an open-todo reminder, a goal continuation, a monitor wake. A settle alone no longer ends it; it ends when a new message starts work after that answer: a person's message, or any delivery, whose own sender the new group then holds (a delivery that joins running work adds its sender). A reply in a covered turn continues the delivery's chain at the next hop, so the chain limit still closes it. ([#13042](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13042), part of #12996) ([#13044](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13044))

**`omo remote send` now goes through the same delivery pipeline as every other send, and `--steer` reads the session once.** A person's message to a session on another device enters `createDeliveryPipeline` with the relay address book's reference for the `<device>/<session>` address, so the CLI no longer builds its own transport call; the relay transport reads the running turn once and steers it, where the CLI used to read it a second time first. A `--steer` to a session that is running nothing still sends nothing. The unused second prompt implementation (`promptRemote`) and its argument check are removed. Which sender kinds each device admits is unchanged. ([#13038](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13038))

**A message to a session on this device that waits on a question now says so, as one to another device does.** The send is still queued, and its `delivery` now carries `waiting_on: { kind: "approval", device }`. `device` is this install's account device, and is absent when the install has no device identity. ([#13035](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13035))

**Every message one session sends another now names the device it was sent from, on this device and across devices alike, and a message from another device counts as the cause of the receiving run's next send the same way a local one does.** When no device id can be read (no device service, or it does not answer), the message still goes and records why it names no device. ([#13034](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13034), part of [#13004](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13004))

**A message sent or handed off to a session on another device now reports its `delivery_id`, `effective_mode` and `endpoint`, as one sent within this device does.** The answer came from the account's session listing and dropped those fields. It now passes the relay transport's own delivery facts through. The `endpoint` is `null` because the sender knows no endpoint on that device. ([#13033](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13033))

**A reply to an agent on another device now reaches it by the id in the message header or by its name, with no prompt on the same account.** One resolver now finds a thread across this device's threads and the account's other devices: an exact durable id, then an account alias, then the name ladder judged over every entry (two d

**Release binaries may be up to 210 MiB.** The 5.1.67 publish stopped on Linux x64 because its binary measured 209,889,456 bytes, 174,256 bytes over the 200 MiB per-binary budget (5.1.66's was 209,664,176). The budget moves to 210 MiB, about 5% above that size, and still fails any release that goes past it; the 5 MiB headroom warning is unchanged. (#13052) ([#13052](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13052))
